svg.title: Changing a catalog, and snapshots
svg.desc: Additions create small sorted segments that merge from the tail while a segment is at least half the one before it; removals are tombstones until a merge or compaction drops the postings. A snapshot stores the id space, the liveness bitmap and every segment's keys, offsets and packed postings behind checksummed headers; a load verifies the checksum and the structure and rebuilds each directory.
svg.text: Segments never change in place: changes build new segments and swap them in, and a snapshot stores the segments as they are.
a sorted segment of its own
merged: at least half of the one before
a tombstone: id 7's postings stay, searches skip
the deltas merge into one; segment 0 is untouched
one segment; id 7's postings are dropped
A merge is one pass over the segments it joins; runs that need
no change are copied as packed bits, without decoding.
Change a clone and swap it in: searches keep the catalog they began on.
live bitmap: a bit per id
Postings are stored packed as in memory, so a file is about the
catalog's size. The directory is not stored; padding is zero.
Loading: every check passes before a catalog exists
The structural checks run on every core for a large segment, and with simd compare a block of postings at a time.
Any failure returns a SnapshotError (truncated, bad magic, unsupported version, checksum mismatch, corrupt structure) and no catalog.
The checksum is a fast 64-bit hash against accidents (truncation, bit rot), not tampering: load files only from where you write them.
Real catalog, 1.94 GiB, two hardware threads: read_from 2.0 s (1.5 s with huge pages), map_from 0.9 s. A mapped catalog keeps
its postings in the page cache, shared between processes; only keys and directories, about a quarter, are on the heap.
